title: Social Choice Function
body_html:
Social Choice Function

A social choice function (SCF) on a population $N$ and alternative set $A$ is a map $$ G : \mathrm{PrefProfile}(N, A) \to A $$ that selects, for every preference profile, a single winning alternative.

In Lean this is the structure SocialChoice.Voting.SCF N A with one field f : PrefProfile N A → A, equipped with a CoeFun so G P is the chosen alternative at profile $P$.

Compared with a social welfare function ([[social_choice.voting.swf]]) the SCF returns only the top-pick rather than a full ranking. The standard axioms — unanimity ([[social_choice.voting.unanimity]]), monotonicity ([[social_choice.voting.monotonic_scf]]), strategy-proofness ([[social_choice.voting.strategyproof]]), and (non-)dictatorship ([[social_choice.voting.dictatorial_scf]]) — are all stated directly on $G(P)$.

References

  • [MSZ 21.21] Maschler, Solan, and Zamir, Game Theory, references/GameTheory.pdf. Social choice function.
